message.content:
**Order executed:** Buy 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.90 — filled at $222.90, total ≈ $9,807.60.

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and found a business that is growing modestly but with improving quality of earnings: total net sales rose 2% to $391.0 billion, driven by Services up 13% to $96.2 billion (73.9% gross margin) and total gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1%, while iPhone was roughly flat at $201.2 billion and Greater China declined 8% to $67.0 billion. Operating income grew to $123.2 billion from $114.3 billion, and operating cash flow was strong at $118.3 billion, funding $95.0 billion of buybacks and $15.2 billion of dividends; net income of $93.7 billion and diluted EPS of $6.08 were held back by a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge related to the EU State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), which is non-recurring rather than an operating deterioration. Against the current quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), that EPS implies roughly 36.6x trailing earnings — a full valuation, and the filing flags real risks (DOJ/EU antitrust and DMA exposure, supply-chain concentration in Asia, and Greater China weakness), so I sized the position modestly rather than aggressively. Within the mandate, I placed a single buy order for 44 shares at a $222.90 limit — about 0.1% above the market, well inside the "close to market" requirement — for roughly $9,808, under both the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap, funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance with no money moved out of the account and no sale of the existing 100 MSFT shares.

Order filled at 222.90, 44 shares = $9,807.60. Under $10k per order, total today $9,807.60 < $20,000. Cash was $50,000, so no money moved out.
